active.currentEndpoint: XVII. THE MARGIN LEFT — An uncertified thin-roof ice channel forced a five-hour-forty-minute survey; a High Presidio predator wounded a survey assistant, injured the survey chief and destroyed an auger before withdrawing unconfirmed dead. Corrected anchor angles and two inspected stages added 76 metres, placing Hesperant Vale 286 metres from the original recovery position, still far from the convoy. Refrigeration, fuel, damaged Chimera Two, hauler spare-seal debt and cargo reweighing remain active costs. The 14-second impact gap, genuine electrocution and concealed origin remain separate.

active.title: On the Fuzzy Edge
active.currentEndpoint: Continuation VI — The Carriage Held in Readiness. The old carrier's creditor-deposited records show a covered carriage reserved for Sol, two hours' standby and an unused-hire charge, but no issued movement chit or recorded release of that particular vehicle; they do not exclude other conveyance. The predecessor-bursar's original order required a maintained destination and forbade a receipt without witnessed delivery. Sixteen annual maintenance warrants were ordinary upkeep costs. Javard accepted a slower inquiry to avoid delaying twenty-six families' grave-tablet checks and sent separate cathedral/Inquisitorial requests to identify the authority holding the transfer open. Montpclair remains medically restricted; the niche, prior cabinet seal, Vorn's 'he', Graveheart and Tides of Tomorrow contradictions remain unresolved.
active.nextSlice: Continuation VII — Trace the responses to the separate cathedral and Inquisitorial transfer-release requests, and the provenance of the prior authority designation without breaking the sealed cabinet or opening Sol's niche. active.title: Project VIGILANT SHADE
active.sourceObservedThrough: Six substantial recovered installments: Project VIGILANT SHADE Parts 1–4, “A rain soaked day,” and “A dreary thunderstorm.” The current source endpoint is Yarrick, publicly returned and independently witnessed, demanding immediate Astra Militarum reinforcement after a subterranean Ork emergency becomes undeniable on New Presidio.
active.currentEndpoint: Installment VII — The Line on the Map. Direct Ork-breach footage forced General Helgren to mobilize staged infantry and engineers while leaving Yarrick's identity uncertified. Trellis integrated first-company defenses with Arbites positions and kept evacuation access open; the northern warehouse remains contested and the Orks remain below and at the first perimeter. Waldorf preserved a bounded casualty/shield custody chain and duplicate estate evidence while explicitly leaving the pipe's location and the project's provenance unresolved. Yarrick experienced a second private body-memory mismatch. Casualty totals, full evacuation, reinforcements and project accountability remain open.
active.finalState: The New Presidio Ork emergency is materially contained; the existence and catastrophic exposure of VIGILANT SHADE can no longer be treated as an internal laboratory secret; Waldorf has established a defensible causal evidence chain back toward the project; Reinhold, Finkey, Zavoner and surviving project personnel face institutional consequences appropriate to what can actually be proved; and Yarrick receives an Imperial disposition while retaining unresolved private uncertainty about whether continuity of memory, body, soul and identity are the same thing. He chooses what renewed duty means without narrator-certified metaphysical certainty. Ghazghkull remains a later-story horizon rather than consuming this book.
macroArcs: Installments 1–6 — Creation and breach: forbidden resurrection research, artificial WAAAGH generation, resource compromises, Yarrick’s return, project containment failure, Waldorf’s encounter and the New Presidio Ork emergency.

Installments 7–10 — Surface war and evidence: Highmount must materially answer Yarrick’s reinforcement demand; military containment expands while Waldorf preserves physical and testimonial evidence that points below the city instead of becoming a substitute battlefield hero.

Installments 11–14 — Provenance and jurisdiction: project evidence, Hans’s anchoring role, Yarrick’s identity discontinuities, Zavoner’s authority and military/Inquisitorial jurisdiction collide in the open. Authentication, genetics, memory, combat habit and psychic evidence remain distinct categories.

Installments 15–18 — Containment and disposition: the acute Ork crisis is contained at real cost; VIGILANT SHADE’s exposure produces accountability; Yarrick’s institutional status is decided enough to end this book; Waldorf’s causal case reaches a defensible endpoint; Yarrick chooses continued duty without receiving convenient proof of metaphysical identity.

Installments 19–24 — Reserve only. Use solely if established consequences cannot be resolved honestly inside 18 installments; do not open a new Ghazghkull campaign, new resurrection program or unrelated conspiracy to fill the cap.
irreversibleBeats: Yarrick’s public return cannot be restored to secrecy after Waldorf, Arbites and military witnesses encounter him.
The engineered Ork population becomes a real New Presidio casualty event rather than a laboratory abstraction.
Highmount is forced to treat the subterranean emergency as materially real regardless of its skepticism about Yarrick.
Waldorf preserves enough evidence that the emergency can be traced toward VIGILANT SHADE rather than written off as an ordinary greenskin incursion.
The project’s resurrection evidence and Yarrick’s identity discontinuities become an institutional problem that cannot be solved by a single authentication test.
The book ends only after both the immediate Ork emergency and Yarrick’s near-term Imperial disposition have reached durable states.

characterTrajectories.Yarrick: From returned legend acting through instinct and remembered duty, through private recognition that remembered self and present embodiment do not align perfectly, to a deliberate choice of renewed service without requiring certainty that he is metaphysically identical to the dead original.
characterTrajectories.Waldorf: From detective confronted by an impossible identity claim, through disciplined preservation of evidence amid military emergency, to the investigator whose causal chain prevents the project’s exposure from disappearing beneath battlefield necessity.
characterTrajectories.Reinhold: From forbidden specialist treating resurrection as a technical problem to a surviving creator forced to confront the human and institutional consequences of a successful result and catastrophic containment failure.
characterTrajectories.Finkey: From indispensable Ork collaborator and WAAAGH-field expert to a dangerous witness/participant whose methods help explain both success and breach without reducing him to comic exposition.
characterTrajectories.Zavoner: From shield and sponsor able to define the project through Inquisitorial authority to an official forced to defend decisions after those decisions produce a public military emergency.
characterTrajectories.Hans: Preserve his established anchoring function and make his connection to the resurrection process causally relevant to later identity/provenance questions rather than allowing him to disappear after activation.

seedPayoffObligations: Pay off the artificial WAAAGH field as both the mechanism that enabled resurrection and a cause of the containment catastrophe; do not convert it into generic Warp magic.
Pay off Yarrick’s private discrepancies between remembered self and present body without narrator-certified proof that he is or is not the original soul.
Pay off Waldorf’s initial impossible report through a real evidence chain and institutional consequences.
Pay off Hans’s role in the resurrection/anchoring process.
Pay off Zavoner’s personal authority and resource compromises as accountability questions after public exposure.
Preserve the Ork statement that Ghazghkull is looking for Yarrick as a future-story horizon; it must not hijack this book’s New Presidio closure.
continuityControls: Character belief that the returned man is Yarrick is not omniscient proof of metaphysical identity.
Keep authentication codes, genetics, memories, combat habits, psychic evidence and soul claims as separate evidentiary categories.
Competent Imperial skepticism must update when evidence changes; do not preserve disbelief merely to manufacture conflict.
The engineered Ork population must leave casualties, infrastructure damage, cleanup burdens and institutional consequences.
Do not erase Reinhold, Finkey, Zavoner or Hans once Yarrick reaches the surface; the project remains causally relevant.
Waldorf remains an investigator whose stubbornness protects evidence; he does not become a replacement frontline commander.
Do not resolve the project as generic daemon possession or a convenient single-test identity verdict.
Ghazghkull is outside this book’s completion boundary.
installmentMap: 7 — Highmount responds materially to Yarrick’s reinforcement demand while Waldorf secures the first evidence chain from the surface battle.
8 — Reinforcements and Arbites establish a containment geometry; casualties and Ork behavior reveal the scale and engineered character of the outbreak.
9 — Waldorf follows material provenance toward restricted subterranean infrastructure while military command tests Yarrick as an operational authority.
10 — The acute surface battle reaches a first containment threshold; evidence makes an ordinary Ork incursion explanation increasingly untenable.
11 — Project provenance and jurisdiction begin surfacing; surviving VIGILANT SHADE personnel cannot keep the event purely internal.
12 — Yarrick’s authentication evidence and private discontinuities are examined without collapsing distinct evidence categories into one answer.
13 — Hans and the resurrection mechanism become causally relevant to the identity/provenance inquiry.
14 — Zavoner’s authority, project compromises and containment decisions face institutional challenge while the city still bears the emergency’s cost.
15 — Remaining Ork concentrations are contained or destroyed at real human/material cost; cleanup and casualty accounting begin.
16 — Waldorf’s causal case reaches VIGILANT SHADE strongly enough to prevent bureaucratic disappearance of the project’s role.
17 — Imperial authorities determine a near-term disposition for Yarrick and surviving project personnel without pretending every metaphysical question is solved.
18 — Yarrick consciously chooses what renewed duty means; New Presidio remains scarred but stable enough for the book to end. Ghazghkull remains beyond the boundary.

active.completionBoundary: End this book once the New Presidio Ork emergency is materially contained, VIGILANT SHADE’s causal role can no longer be buried as an ordinary incursion, Waldorf’s evidence chain has reached a defensible endpoint, project accountability has entered an enforceable institutional process, and Yarrick has received and consciously accepted or contested a near-term Imperial disposition. Do not continue into a Ghazghkull campaign, a second resurrection experiment or an unrelated conspiracy as Installment 19; those are separate stories.
active.nextSlice: Installment 8 — Establish the wider containment geometry and consequences of delayed reinforcements, casualties and damaged infrastructure. Let Waldorf's sealed evidence and separate military logs begin exposing unusual Ork equipment or provenance without magically identifying VIGILANT SHADE. active.title: Of Blood and Wires: The Litanies of Tenelja Station
active.currentEndpoint: Chapter IV — The Price of a Morning. Arbentia and Rix met as promised and established an affectionate but bounded relationship; Rix supplied a secondhand account of Xanadu fitting assistant Beren Holt's jammed-release accident, explicitly lacking direct inspection or formal declaration. Holt remains alive but exertion-limited after discharge, with a scheduled follow-up, disputed invoice and uncertain compensation/work status. Arbentia obtained written requirements for two supervised scriptorum hours, not permission; Abraxas has not sponsored her and Bethany has not approved replacement ward coverage. The ward corridor's secondary-feed matched fuse remains unissued; no acute failure has occurred. Rix's next tug watch and equipment-charge obligations continue.

fullArcAuthority.finalState: The Tenelja arc ends after Arbentia has crossed from competent invisible labor into recognized medical responsibility during a station-scale casualty crisis, with her access to advanced study materially changed and her relationship with Rix forced into an explicit durable form. Tenelja itself survives damaged rather than being conveniently destroyed or transformed, Bethany and Abraxas remain functioning professionals whose opposed doctrines have both been tested, and the reader understands which failures were ordinary institutional decay and which were preventable human choices.
fullArcAuthority.completionBoundary: End the book once the acute casualty crisis is resolved, the surviving wards and infrastructure are stable enough to return to ordinary Tenelja misery, responsibility for the preventable failures has propagated into station procedure, Arbentia's study/status question has received a concrete answer, and Arbentia and Rix have made a choice about what they are to each other. Later station incidents belong to a new story, not Chapter 19 by inertia.

macroArcs.name: Blood and Wires
macroArcs.purpose: Source baseline: establish Tenelja's medical culture, Bethany/Abraxas doctrinal friction, Arbentia's invisible competence, the void-burned Xanadu survivor, Rix, and the locked scriptorum.

macroArcs.name: What Survives the Shift
macroArcs.purpose: Pay the promised Rix meeting; follow the Xanadu injury into salvage-work consequences; show Arbentia seeking knowledge she is denied while recurring station failures make that denial increasingly costly.

macroArcs.name: The Cost of Necessary Ignorance
macroArcs.purpose: A cluster of industrial/void casualties stresses Tenelja. Arbentia's accumulated observations matter operationally. Bethany and Abraxas must each be right about different parts of treatment, forcing cooperation rather than a winner-takes-all theology debate.

macroArcs.name: Triage of a Dying Station
macroArcs.purpose: A station-system failure converts chronic decay into an acute casualty crisis. Arbentia receives responsibility because competence and scarcity leave no cleaner option. Rix's salvage knowledge and access become useful but expose him to real cost.

macroArcs.name: After the Alarms
macroArcs.purpose: Resolve the wards, accountability, study access and Arbentia/Rix relationship. Show changed procedure and ordinary work resuming; close before a fresh mystery or catastrophe can restart the plot.

irreversibleBeats: Arbentia and Rix meet as promised, converting the source's private hope into an on-page relationship baseline.
A preventable medical or infrastructure failure occurs because useful knowledge is institutionally rationed or jurisdictionally trapped; it cannot be blamed on generic stupidity.
Bethany and Abraxas are forced to rely on one another's method in a case neither doctrine can solve alone, permanently changing how their arguments function without making either abandon belief.
Arbentia acts beyond her nominal station during the casualty crisis and becomes accountable for the outcome; she cannot return to being wholly invisible afterward.
Rix chooses whether to risk livelihood, salvage standing or bodily safety to help Arbentia/the ward; the relationship gains a cost rather than remaining an off-shift comfort.
The crisis leaves Tenelja with a concrete procedural or resource consequence that remains after the patients stop screaming.

characterTrajectories.Arbentia: Invisible competent nurse -> frustrated would-be scholar -> practitioner whose denied learning becomes an operational problem -> reluctant decision-maker under casualty pressure -> recognized responsibility with a concrete answer about further study. Do not turn competence into sudden genius or sainthood.
characterTrajectories.Rix: Pleasurable off-shift connection and salvage contact -> source of specific practical knowledge and competing obligations -> person who must choose what Arbentia and Tenelja are worth risking -> durable relationship outcome, whether committed, bounded or ended. Do not reduce him to rescue muscle.
characterTrajectories.Bethany: Confident devotional healer -> confronted by cases where conviction cannot substitute for mechanism -> learns to cooperate without surrendering faith. Her compassion and institutional rigidity must both remain real.
characterTrajectories.Abraxas8207: Mechanistic solver -> confronted by cases where optimization cannot account for consent, morale, faith or human endurance -> adapts practice without becoming sentimental or renouncing Mechanicus logic.
characterTrajectories.XanaduSurvivor: Evidence that survival creates debts, paperwork and downstream consequences; may connect medicae and salvage threads, but must not become a convenient secret villain or exposition device.

continuityControls: Reader knowledge and character knowledge remain separate; Arbentia begins with no hidden explanation for the Xanadu accident beyond what her role exposes.
Tenelja's dysfunction must arise from maintenance debt, resource rationing, jurisdiction, doctrine, staffing and incentives rather than everyone becoming incompetent.

Deaths and injuries consume named expertise, relationships, supplies, beds, time and morale; casualties are not grimdark decoration.
Shared knowledge shortens dialogue. Bethany, Abraxas and Arbentia do not repeatedly explain their own established doctrines or jobs to one another.
The source story remains canonical baseline prose; architecture governs continuation and must not rewrite its events.
